ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two six-membered carbon rings connected by a middle carbon-carbon connection. The left side is a benzene/cyclohexadiene-like ring, and the lower right of the ring is connected to a nitrogen bearing H; the right side is a cyclohexene-like six-membered ring, and on its lower right side there is an NH bearing H. The curved arrows in the figure mark electron migration: the lone pair of the right NH points toward the adjacent ring carbon, the adjacent π bond in the right ring moves toward the middle C-C connection, and the related π electrons on the left side then point toward the lower-left N-H connection position. Reasoning: Change bond orders in sequence according to the arrows, first forming a C=N imine bond from the right NH and the adjacent ring carbon; then move the adjacent π bond through the central C-C bond; finally form a C=N imine bond with the lower N outside the left ring. The two six-membered carbon skeletons in the product are still connected through the same carbon-carbon bond, the left benzene-derived ring is retained as a cyclohexadiene-type C=CC=C fragment, and overall a neutral diimine product is obtained. Therefore the corresponding SMILES is N=C(CCCC1)C1C2C(C=CC=C2)=N.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure and mark the atoms involved in the arrows. After these bond-order changes, keep the two six-membered carbon frameworks connected at the same carbon-carbon bond and encode the final neutral diimine product as `N=C(CCCC1)C1C2C(C=CC=C2)=N`.
